Title: Honk's Mysterious Visits
Content: My family lives on a farm. My dad is a forest ranger, and my mom is an artist who paints signs for local businesses. She also likes to paint nature scenes.
“Adam, why don't you go outside?” Mom suggested. “There is a nice breeze, so you can fly your dragon kite in the yard. Maybe some friends will pass by.”

“Okay,” I said. When I walked into our yard with my kite, the only thing I saw was our neighbor's goose, Honk. The feathery white bird was a little scary. He flapped his wings and strutted around his yard like he was a king. I decided to keep my distance.

Unfortunately, Honk did not have the same plan. When he spied me and my kite, he flew in my direction. I escaped into the garage and found some sidewalk chalk to play with instead. Then, I happily drew pictures on our front driveway, where Honk could not see me.

That afternoon, Honk paid me another visit. I was standing inside my house looking out through the glass doors to the yard, watching some squirrels play in the oak trees. Suddenly, Honk flapped into our yard and marched up to the doors. He honked at me and pecked the glass with his beak.
Mom heard the noisy bird and called Ms. Lee, Honk's owner. Mom nicely asked Ms. Lee to come and fetch Honk.
“I'm sorry Honk is being a pest,” Ms. Lee apologized. “Usually, his favorite place is my pond.” Ms. Lee came over and scooted Honk home. She waved her arms while walking behind him.
An `text(hour)` later, Honk visited our family again. He seemed happy as he danced in front of the glass doors. I slowly stepped outside to see if I could make friends with him.
In a blink, Honk's cheerful mood disappeared and he started honking at me. Ms. Lee was working in her garden. She heard Honk's yelling and raced over to rescue me.
“I do not know why Honk keeps leaving his pond,” Ms. Lee said with a sigh. “I've never had this problem with him before.”

That afternoon, Honk came to visit us `text(two)` more times. I noticed that he always seemed happy when he arrived, but he did not like when I stepped outside. I tried taking off my hat. I even changed my bright red shirt for a plain white `text(one)`. Honk still scolded me, and Ms. Lee had to herd him home `text(each time)` he came over.

After dinner, Mom offered to fly my dragon kite with me. We were in the yard when Honk made yet another visit to our home. With narrowed eyes, I watched as he bowed his head and danced around in front of the glass doors.

Suddenly, my eyes caught a glimpse of another dancing goose. It was Honk's reflection. He could see himself in our glass doors. I had solved the mystery-Honk was visiting us because he was looking for a friend.
Eagerly, Mom and I went to tell Ms. Lee about my discovery.
“Honk must be lonely,” Ms. Lee said. “It is time for me to get a real friend for him.”
“Honk will like that,” I said. “He really wants some company.”
“My brother Mark has a flock of geese on his farm,” Ms. Lee said next. “Would you like to come and help me pick out a partner for Honk? You could meet Mark's son, Tanner, too.”

Mom agreed with the plan, so I gave Ms. Lee a great big “Yes!” Honk had showed me something important. He was willing to leave his pond to make new discoveries. It was time for me to be adventurous too.
